---
title: "Rename the CLI executable from pairmerge to pairloom (as executed)"
author: "Yun Jiang"
date: today
---

# Objective

Replace the executable name `pairmerge` with `pairloom` everywhere the
user-facing surface names the command, per the user's explicit instruction
("use pairloom instead of pairmerge"). The Python package was already
`pairloom`; only the console-script name, program identification, message
prefixes, and documentation change. Historical records under `docs/plans/`
keep the name that was true when they were written.

# Scope

1. `pyproject.toml` `[project.scripts]`: `pairmerge` -> `pairloom`.
2. `src/pairloom/cli.py`: module docstring, `prog=`, note/warning/error
   message prefixes.
3. `src/pairloom/pipeline.py`: stderr summary/warning prefixes and the
   `@PG` header records (ID/PN/CL) — a visible output change.
4. `tests/test_cli.py` entry-point tests and `tests/conftest.py` docstring.
5. `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `pixi.toml` `cli` task,
   `data/synthetic/EXPECTED.md`.
6. Regenerate `data/synthetic/expected_*` outputs: the committed BAMs embed
   `@PG ID:pairmerge PN:pairmerge`, which changes with the rename.
7. Refresh the pixi env (`pixi install`) so the console script is
   regenerated under the new name.
8. Update the project-overview memory to keep it truthful.

# Risks

- Stale `pairmerge` script lingering in the pixi env after the entry-point
  change: verify with `shutil.which` both ways; reinstall if needed.
- Tests asserting the old name or prefix: full suite run must stay green
  (182 expected).
- Byte-level output change of `@PG`-bearing BAMs is intended, not a
  regression; the committed expected outputs are regenerated in the same
  commit so the tree stays consistent.

# Verification

1. `pixi install`; `pairloom --help` and `pairloom --version` work;
   `pairmerge` no longer resolves in the pixi env.
2. `pixi run test` green (182), `pixi run lint` / `pixi run format` clean.
3. Synthetic dataset regenerated; `git diff` on `data/synthetic/` shows
   only the `@PG` rename and expected-content equality otherwise.
4. `git grep pairmerge` over tracked sources returns hits only in
   historical `docs/plans/` records.
